clue.text: Source of friction, and not just in open-air entertainment

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, so only its opening letter is used

parts.note: something not just is unfair

explanation.surface: Somebody complains that rubbing and unfairness spoil an outdoor show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source of' takes the first letter F from 'friction'; 'and' and 'in' are only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelling fair with rides and stalls is a typical outdoor amusement.

clue.text: It may be described as time to throw him out — no friends!

definitions.text: It may be described as time

indicators.note: to throw letters is to scatter them into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone wants to eject a man who has no friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throw' rearranges all fifteen letters of HIM OUT NO FRIENDS; 'out' is part of the fodder, not the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Physics treats time as the extra coordinate beyond length, breadth and height.

clue.text: Small children becoming pickpockets

explanation.surface: Little ones turning into thieves.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for young kids, and also for petty thieves who nip purses.

clue.text: Eagle and bear reunited in harmony

indicators.note: the letters of eagle and bear are brought together again in a new order

explanation.surface: Two animals get back together and are friends.
explanation.definitionFit: People who are agreeable to a plan are in accord with it.

clue.text: Inform on people in struggle for position

parts.note: to rat on someone is to inform on them
a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: A grass betrays others in a fight to get ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: The competitive scramble of modern working life is a fierce contest for status.

clue.text: Robert Crosby is jumping up and down

parts.note: Bob is the usual short form of the name Robert
Bing Crosby was the American crooner

explanation.surface: A man called Robert Crosby is leaping about.
explanation.definitionFit: Bobbing describes moving quickly up and down, like a float on water.

clue.text: Put last of beer into mug and wave

indicators.note: into places the last letter inside the mug word

parts.note: a beaker is a drinking mug

indicators.note: last of points to the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Pour the dregs of the ale into a cup and salute.
explanation.definitionFit: A large wave crashing on the shore is a breaker.

clue.text: Waits for offers covering insurance — at last

indicators.note: covering means the offers word wraps round the extra letter

parts.note: bids are offers at auction

indicators.note: at last signals the final letter of insurance

explanation.surface: An insurer waits for quotes that protect them.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide or stay is to wait.

clue.text: Copy? One friend swallowed it!

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: swallowed means the friend word takes the next word inside it

parts.note: mate is a friend

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a pal really gulped it down.
explanation.definitionFit: To mimic or reproduce someone's actions is to copy them.

clue.text: Good former workers fish for this!

definitions.text: Good former workers fish for this!

parts.note: olden means of former times
hands are manual workers
hake is a sea fish

explanation.surface: Retired staff go angling for a farewell reward.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: departing workers angle for a generous severance payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A generous severance payment to a departing executive or employee.

clue.text: Illegal stimulant possibly found in shoe

explanation.surface: Some banned drug may have been smuggled inside footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for an amphetamine pill, and also the top part of footwear above the sole.

clue.text: Mild alert broke the day-to-day grind

indicators.note: the words mild alert are broken apart and their letters reassembled

explanation.surface: A gentle warning interrupted the monotony of routine work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broke' rearranges the nine letters of MILD ALERT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tedious, repetitive routine is figuratively a mill wheel walked on endlessly.

clue.text: Hyde, perhaps, followed subject into recreation area

indicators.note: the word for Hyde comes after the word for subject

parts.note: a theme is the subject of a talk or piece
Hyde Park in London is one example of a park

explanation.surface: Mr Hyde trailed a topic into a leisure ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Hyde Park is a large public park in central London; 'Hyde' tempts the solver towards Jekyll and Hyde.
explanation.definitionFit: An amusement complex built around a single idea is a leisure venue.

clue.text: Old and initially sad story

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: An ancient and gloomy narrative.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread or news that is no longer fresh is described as old.

clue.text: Deuterium can cripple

parts.note: D is the chemical symbol for deuterium, heavy hydrogen
can means is able

explanation.surface: Heavy hydrogen is capable of maiming someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To cripple a machine or person is to put them out of action.

clue.text: Judge about to call for quiet — and give life again to…

parts.note: a referee, ref for short, judges a match
re is Latin-derived for about or concerning
sh is the noise made to ask for silence

explanation.surface: A referee is about to ask for silence before reviving the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs this clue on into the next one, a surface link only.
explanation.definitionFit: To revive or reinvigorate something is to make it lively once more.

clue.text: Two elements making for strong drink

parts.note: fire is one of the four classical elements
water is another of the classical elements

explanation.surface: Two of the classical elements combine to produce hard liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirits such as whisky were nicknamed so for their burning strength.

clue.text: …manipulator for criminal arms use

indicators.note: a criminal use of the words arms use twists them into a new order

explanation.surface: A masseur is somehow linked to illegal use of weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who kneads muscles with their hands is a body manipulator.

clue.text: A bargain, darling? Just a bit!

parts.note: a snip is British slang for a bargain
pet is a term of endearment, like darling

explanation.surface: A shopper calls a cheap buy a small treat.
explanation.definitionFit: A small extract or fragment is only a little piece.

clue.text: Another performance from salesman — get up!

parts.note: rep is short for a sales representative
to rise is to get up

explanation.surface: A salesman tells the audience to stand for an encore.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeated piece of music or a revival of a show.

clue.text: Short? A fashionable drape

parts.note: curt means short or brusque
in means fashionable, as in the in thing

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a trendy hanging fabric is too short.
explanation.definitionFit: A window hanging of fabric is called a drape, especially in American usage.

clue.text: Keeps bags to cover empty till

indicators.note: to cover means the bags word goes round the letters from till

parts.note: cases are bags for luggage

indicators.note: empty removes the inside of till leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone holds on to sacks to hide a cleared-out cash drawer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeps' looks like a verb; it is the noun for fortified towers.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeps are fortified towers, so fortresses are castles.

clue.text: Sounds like a rule to put on a charge

indicators.note: sounds like means the words are spoken and heard as the answer

parts.note: a reign is a period of rule

explanation.surface: A regulation seems to accuse someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring someone before a court to answer a charge.

clue.text: Fixes trouble between points

indicators.note: between places the trouble word inside the two compass letters

parts.note: N and S are compass points, north and south
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: Someone repairs a problem caught between two sharp ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail something down is to fix or secure it.

clue.text: Cancel credit in advance

indicators.note: in places the credit letters inside the advance word

parts.note: a sub is a payment in advance of wages
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: Someone pays upfront and then calls off the deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrub a plan is to call it off.

clue.text: They're said to be at cross purposes

definitions.text: They're said to be at cross purposes

parts.words: They're said to be at cross purposes
parts.note: secret words a guard demands are spoken for the purpose of crossing a checkpoint, not for disagreement

explanation.surface: Some remarks seem to cause misunderstanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At cross purposes' usually means misunderstanding each other; here it means for the purpose of crossing a sentry line.
explanation.definitionFit: Secret code words are spoken to sentries so a person may pass across a guarded line.

clue.text: Just a mail trip that went wrong!

indicators.note: the letters of a mail trip go astray and land in a new order

explanation.surface: A postal round that failed was only that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like 'merely'; it is the adjective meaning fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A fair, unbiased judgement is just.

clue.text: Identification mark kept one inside a Russian forest

indicators.note: kept means the label word holds the numeral within it

parts.note: a tag is a label identifying something
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A labelled marker was left in a Siberian woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept ... inside' puts I in TAG; A is then added on.
explanation.definitionFit: The subarctic coniferous woodland of Siberia is called by this Russian word.

clue.text: Distinguished peer accepted thanks

indicators.note: accepted means the peer word takes the thanks word inside it

parts.note: a noble is a peer of the realm
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: An eminent lord received gratitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone remarkable or eminent is worthy of note.

clue.text: Set out and called in — odd!

indicators.note: in places the called word inside the rearranged letters
out signals that the letters of set are laid out in a different order

parts.note: the word set, to be rearranged
rang means telephoned or called

explanation.surface: Someone set off and phoned home, which seemed peculiar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SET as STE, and 'in' puts RANG inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something peculiar or unusual is odd.
